title: Tool, resource, or prompt?
intro: The confusable triple, as a sorting bench. Side effects? Initiative? Recipe? File each capability.

cards.text: search_papers — query arXiv and store results to disk
Send a message to a Slack channel
Update a record in the CRM
papers://folders — the list of saved topic folders
papers://{topic} — the stored info for a topic, filled at runtime
An API response cached as read-only JSON with a mime type
A well-tested 'summarize this transcript' message template

debrief: Run the decision rule: anything that acts or writes (search-and-store, send, update) is a tool — the model reaches for it mid-conversation. Anything that only hands back existing data (folder lists, stored topic info, cached responses) is a resource — GET-like, no side effects, addressed by URI, pulled in by the app or user. Anything that packages a great interaction (summary templates, crafted search instructions) is a prompt — authored and tested once on the server, triggered by the user. The trap card is c1: it *mentions papers* like the resources do, but it writes to disk — side effects make it a tool.
